title: What I Learned Building and Marketing Rate My Form for Shipaton 2026
content_md: I always wanted to build a health and fitness app, That was the whole reason little me wanted to become an app developer. I came across calisthenics in my late teens and getting into it was one of the best things that happened to me. The cool calisthenics skills always left me in complete shock. When I started, there weren’t many calisthenics apps out there, so I used general workout apps like Strong and Hevy. Logging sets was easy. Real form feedback and clear progression were not. In my early 20s, after I’d grasped Android development, I built a personal project on pose detection and exercise form coaching. That led to work on a medical workplace posture correction app for Android and iOS, where I learned a lot about biomechanics and movement analysis. Feeling stuck creatively, I was scrolling Reddit when I came across Shipaton. I read through the contest details, and suddenly I just knew what I had to build. Taking inspiration from anime and calisthenics, I built Rate My Form . It’s simple: record your exercise form, let on-device ML analyze the movements, and generate tips and coaching cues to help you fix inaccuracies and improve your form and reps. I also put the biomechanical knowledge I learned on that work app to use, and based on it, I developed algorithms to detect whether a user’s muscles are in tension zones and how much they actually worked the muscle.
